subject: SIG follow-up: access controls evidence (SAML/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@acme-cloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-cloud.com
Date: 2026-10-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG intake: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - request for evidence

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. We're collecting artifacts to finish our SIG assessment and have a few focused asks on access controls:

1) SSO/SAML: sample SAML metadata, assertion attributes (NameID format you recommend), and confirmation that IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows are supported.
2) SCIM: SCIM provisioning scope (users/groups), sample provisioning logs for a user create/update, and how failures are surfaced to customers.
3) RBAC: current role matrix (roles -> permissions) and whether least-privilege is enforced by default.
4) MFA: where MFA is enforced (console, admin UI, API), and how you handle service accounts/non-interactive credentials.

If you can attach artifacts or point us to a Drive folder, that would help us close the SIG quickly. Ideally we need these by Oct 12 to hit our compliance deadline.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
Security Engineer, Acme Cloud

Attachments: Acme-SIG-Request-20261001.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - initial artifacts

Hi Maria,

Thanks — we can absolutely provide these. I've started a small evidence bundle and attached an initial answers doc with high-level confirmations. Quick notes up front:

- SSO/SAML: We support both IdP- and SP-initiated SAML. Default NameID we recommend is transient or email (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress) depending on your provisioning needs; we can include sample metadata and an example assertion.
- SCIM: We support SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning. I'll include a redacted provisioning log and a short explanation of error handling (retries and webhook alerts).
- RBAC: Attached is a draft role-permission matrix. By default, out-of-the-box roles are scoped for least privilege; customers can create custom roles.
- MFA: Strong MFA is enforced for interactive console/admin access for all accounts. We require workspace admins to enable MFA; for API/service accounts we recommend scoped API keys with limited lifetimes and optional OAuth with service-to-service certs.

Attachments included: initial-sig-answers.md (doc stub). We still need to pull the SCIM CSV logs and final RBAC matrix — Dev is on that. I'll also drop a Drive link with the evidence bundle once we have the logs.

If you want a short call to walk through before you load into your tooling, happy to schedule.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Jordan Blake
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG intake: access controls (SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA) - RBAC matrix draft

Maria / Jordan,

Attaching the RBAC draft matrix for your review. Notes: roles are split into Viewer / Developer / Operator / Admin. Permission rules are additive; the default for newly created workspaces is Viewer-only until an admin grants elevated roles. We intentionally lock down certain admin actions (model deployment, billing) behind the Admin role.

Attachment: rbac_matrix_draft.xlsx (excel stub)

A couple of implementation details for your SIG:
- Least privilege: we ship with restrictive defaults and a policy that new users have no elevated rights. Customers must explicitly grant higher roles (no implicit admin).
- Auditing: every role change generates an audit event retained per the customer's retention policy; we can export a sample audit for the SIG.

I'll run the SCIM log export this afternoon and post the CSV to the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG intake: access controls (follow-up questions)

Jordan / Dev — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions before we mark items as answered:

1) For SAML assertions, do you support persistent NameID for use cases where Acme wants a stable immutable identifier? If so, any recommendations on attribute mapping (email vs employeeID)?
2) For SCIM sync failures: how are provisioning errors surfaced to customers? Does Redwood push webhook notifications or do we need to poll logs?
3) For service accounts: you mentioned OAuth with certs. Do you support MFA or 2FA for service-to-service tokens, or is that out of scope? We need an attestation of how service accounts are protected from misuse.

We'd prefer a succinct answer plus the artifact (sample assertion and log) rather than a long doc.

-Maria

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake: access controls (answers + artifacts)

Hi Maria,

Answers inline and attached artifacts below. Short version up front: we support persistent NameID, SCIM failure alerts via webhook + UI alerts, and service accounts are protected via scoped API keys and optional short-lived cert-based OAuth; MFA is not applied to non-interactive tokens but is enforced on all interactive admin access.

1) SAML NameID: We support both transient and persistent NameID (persistent recommended for immutable identifiers). Recommended mapping: use Acme employeeID as persistent NameID if you need a stable key; falling back to email is acceptable if employeeIDs are not available. Attached: sample-saml-assertion.xml (redacted).

2) SCIM failures: Provisioning errors are surfaced two ways:
   - Webhook: configuration allows your SCIM endpoint to receive push failure notifications with status and error codes.
   - Admin UI & Logs: provisioning errors are visible in the Redwood Console under Provisioning -> Events; we also provide a downloadable CSV export.
Attached: scim-sync-log-20261005.csv (redacted sample export).

3) Service accounts and MFA: Non-interactive service accounts use either long-lived API keys (not recommended) or short-lived OAuth tokens obtained via a client credentials flow paired with rotating certificates. We require an explicit approval workflow to create high-privilege service accounts and log all token grants in the audit trail. For highest assurance, we advise using short-lived certs + mTLS where possible; MFA (interactive 2FA) is not applied to automated tokens but issuance requires an admin with MFA-locked console access.

Drive link with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-SIG-Evidence

Attachments: sample-saml-assertion.xml, scim-sync-log-20261005.csv

Let us know if you'd like a 20-minute walkthrough; we can demo the Provisioning events UI and the RBAC assignment flow.

Best,
Jordan

Hi Maria,

Just adding a short note on audit retention and role change approvals:

- Audit retention: audit events (role changes, token grants, SSO events) are retained per customer-configured policy; standard retention is 365 days for hosted customers.
- Role change approvals: we offer optional role-approval workflows (two approver model) for elevated roles — if you enable the workflow, role grants require explicit approval and that approval is recorded in the audit entry.

I'll attach a redacted audit export if you'd like; otherwise, Jordan and Dev's artifacts should get you over the line.

Thanks,
